findings.title: TopicsController#unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser record
findings.body: In the new `unsubscribe` action, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (any logged-in user can visit /t/<any topic>/unsubscribe for a topic they have never viewed, posted in, or been emailed about — the URL is trivially guessable since it is just the topic URL plus /unsubscribe). The code then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. The action should create/normalize the record via `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` like `set_notifications` does, which also correctly sets `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` and publishes the MessageBus `notification_level_change` event that the direct `tu.save!` path skips.

findings.title: State-changing GET endpoint is vulnerable to CSRF and accidental triggering
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action mutates the user's notification level on a GET request. A logged-in user's browser can be made to hit this URL cross-site (e.g. an `` on an attacker page sends session cookies), silently muting or un-muting topics for the victim. Additionally, because the handler *toggles* state (watching/tracking -> regular, otherwise -> muted), any repeated visit — a page refresh, browser pre-render/prefetch of the email link, or a scanner following links in an open session — flips the user's notification level again, potentially re-subscribing someone who just unsubscribed. State changes should be made via a POST endpoint (the email link can go to a page with a button, or use a per-user token), not on GET.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking any email builder caller that doesn't pass it
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder` merges its opts into template_args, so any caller using `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationData` when building the body (`body << I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`) or the HTML part, and the email will fail to send. This is an undocumented new contract on the MessageBuilder API — nothing enforces or documents that `unsubscribe_url` must accompany `add_unsubscribe_link`, so plugins or future mailers that only pass `add_unsubscribe_link` will break. The builder should default `unsubscribe_url` (e.g. fall back to the preferences URL) or omit that sentence when it is absent, and this requirement needs a test.

findings.title: Unsubscribe toggle does not actually unsubscribe watching/tracking users, contradicting the email text
findings.body: The controller demotes watching/tracking users only to `regular` on the first click. At the `regular` notification level the user still receives notifications when they are replied to, mentioned, or quoted, yet the email footer added in this PR says "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here" and the client page says "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>". A watching user who clicks the unsubscribe link in the email will keep getting reply/mention emails for that topic. If the intent is a toggle, the messaging is wrong; if the intent is unsubscribe, the level should go to `muted` (or the UI should make the choice explicit before mutating).

findings.title: No tests for the new TopicsController#unsubscribe behavior
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action implements toggle semantics, slug-mismatch 301 redirects, permission handling, and TopicUser mutation, but no request/controller specs were added for any of it (the only test touched in the PR is the message_builder spec, which merely adds an `unsubscribe_url` option without asserting the topic link appears in the body or List-Unsubscribe header). Given the reachable nil crash and the CSRF-prone GET noted above, this endpoint needs specs covering: user with no TopicUser record, watching vs regular vs muted starting levels, wrong-slug redirect, and inaccessible topic.
